chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us, from his father, who said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Inform me of the death of Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him):
He said: When his appointed time came, his term was fulfilled, and his sustenance was cut off, the Angel of Death came to him and said to him: "Peace be upon you, O one whom Allah spoke to."

Musa said: "And upon you be peace. Who are you?" He said: "I am the Angel of Death." He said: "What has brought you?" He said: "I have come to take your soul." Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "From where will you take my soul?" He said: "From your mouth." Musa (peace be upon him) said: "How, when I have spoken to my Lord, the Majestic, with it!" He said: "Then from your hands." He said: "How, when I have carried the Torah with them!" He said: "Then from your feet." He said: "How, when I have trodden upon Mount Sinai with them!" He said: "Then from your eyes?" He said: "How, when they have not ceased gazing toward my Lord with hope!" He said: "Then from your ears." He said: "How, when I have heard the speech of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, with them!"

He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to the Angel of Death: Do not take his soul until he himself desires it. The Angel of Death departed, and Musa (peace be upon him) remained as long as Allah willed after that.

And he buried him in the grave, and leveled the earth upon him. The one who was digging the grave was an angel in the form of a human. That was in the wilderness. Then a caller called out from the sky: 'Musa the one who spoke to Allah has died! So which soul will not die?'

And my father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his father, peace be upon them, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was asked about the grave of Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him, where it is.
He said: 'It is near the great road, by the red sand dune.'

key_terms.الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر: Enjoining good and forbidding evil, a fundamental Islamic duty
key_terms.الزبانية: Angels of punishment who guard Hell
key_terms.الصراط: The Path/Bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the good deeds that save people on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) described a series of visions he saw, each depicting how a specific good deed -- such as honoring parents, ablution, dhikr, prayer, fasting, ghusl, Hajj, maintaining family ties, charity, enjoining good, good character, fear of God, deceased children, hope in God, tears of humility, good opinion of God, sending blessings upon the Prophet, and the shahada -- intervenes to save a person from trials of death, the grave, and the Day of Judgment. This famous hadith, narrated by the companion Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura at a gathering with the Prophet in Medina, served as comprehensive moral instruction cataloguing the salvific power of righteous deeds in the Hereafter.
